description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer web protocols (HTTP/HTTPS) to blend into existing outbound traffic. Low-and-slow periodic beaconing mimics benign heartbeat connections, frequently exhibiting consistent inter-arrival times (IAT).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Deploy network intrusion detection and prevention systems capable of identifying repeated beacon patterns and anomalous TLS session parameters.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Enforce outbound proxy filtering, inspect HTTPS headers/SNI, and block direct IP-based web requests that bypass DNS.

description: Adversaries may use the Domain Name System (DNS) protocol for command and control signaling and data tunneling. High frequency of TXT/NULL record queries, high Shannon entropy subdomains, and oversized DNS payloads indicate tunneling activity.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic (DNS Filtering)
mitigations.description: Route all internal DNS traffic through hardened internal resolvers; sinkhole newly registered domains and block unauthorized outbound UDP/TCP port 53.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Inspect DNS query lengths and entropy to flag tunneled text/hex data in labels.

technique_name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted/Non-C2 Protocol
description: Adversaries may steal data by encoding it inside standard non-C2 network protocols such as DNS, ICMP, or covert channels to circumvent data loss prevention (DLP) controls.

mitigations.name: Data Loss Prevention
mitigations.description: Monitor and restrict outbound volumetric flows across unconventional channels.

description: Adversaries may abuse Server Message Block (SMB) and administrative shares (e.g., C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) to transfer files, execute commands remotely, and propagate laterally across internal subnets.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.description: Segment internal workstation networks from servers and restrict workstation-to-workstation SMB communications via host firewalls.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Disable default administrator shares and prevent domain admin accounts from authenticating to non-domain controller endpoints.

description: Adversaries may use Secure Shell (SSH) connections with compromised credentials or stolen private keys to log into internal hosts and move laterally across enterprise systems.

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
mitigations.description: Require MFA for SSH bastions and use certificate-based or hardware token authentication instead of passwords.

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.description: Restrict SSH ingress to designated management jump boxes.

description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell (a Living-off-the-Land binary) to execute malicious code in memory without dropping executables to disk, frequently spawning suspicious outbound network connections.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.description: Enforce PowerShell Constrained Language Mode (CLM) and deploy application control policies such as AppLocker/WDAC.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.description: Enable PowerShell script block logging (Event ID 4104) and transcription logging.

description: Adversaries abuse Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to execute malicious tasks and orchestrate stealthy lateral operations via RPC/DCOM.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Limit local administrative rights and restrict remote WMI access via RPC endpoint filtering.

description: Adversaries negotiate encrypted sessions (e.g., custom TLS configurations or self-signed certificates) to shield command and control payloads from deep packet inspection.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Perform TLS fingerprinting (JA3/JA4) and inspect certificate validity, issuance authority, and SNI discrepancies.

description: Adversaries perform network denial of service (DoS) attacks targeting external network services or internal network infrastructure to cause unavailability through high packet rates or resource exhaustion.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Implement upstream rate limiting, SYN flood cookies, and cloud-based DDoS scrubbing centers.

description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to systematically guess user credentials across protocols such as SSH, RDP, FTP, or HTTP forms.

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.description: Implement account lockout thresholds, progressive login delays, and enforce multi-factor authentication.

description: Adversaries attempt to discover open network services and listening ports across remote hosts using tools like Nmap, scanning multiple destination ports in a short duration.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Configure stateful firewalls to detect port sweeps and automatically blacklist offending source IPs.

description: Adversaries take advantage of vulnerabilities in Internet-facing applications (SQL injection, XSS, RCE) to establish initial footholds.

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.description: Deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF) to inspect payload content for injection signatures.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.description: Maintain a rigorous vulnerability patch management schedule for all public web services.

description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Service Control Manager or tools like PsExec to execute commands remotely or escalate privileges.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Restrict remote service creation privileges to dedicated administrative workstations.

description: Adversaries may compromise third-party systems or botnet nodes to coordinate distributed denial of service or proxy malicious command channels.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Filter traffic to known botnet controller C2 IP and domain blocklists.

description: Adversaries may manipulate products or network delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by final consumers to achieve infiltration.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.description: Verify code signatures and cryptographic hashes of third-party dependencies.

description: Adversaries may employ a cryptographic algorithm to conceal command and control traffic.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Inspect TLS handshake parameters and JA3/JA4 fingerprints.

description: Adversaries may steal data by sending it via an alternative protocol to avoid detection.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Block unauthorized egress protocols from internal servers.
